item.content:encoded:
MLB playoff predictions 2026: Expert picks for every ALDS, NLDS series originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
October has officially arrived, just in time for the MLB postseason to ramp up.
With all four Wild Card series now over — three of which ended in two-game sweeps — just eight teams remain alive in the pursuit of a World Series title, with the Guardians, Rays, Dodgers and Brewers entering the picture after watching the first round from home.
Some of baseball's biggest stars, from Shohei Ohtani and Jacob Misiorowski to Junior Caminero and Cam Schlittler, will be on full display for the division series. On both sides of the bracket, the question will be whether the teams carrying their Wild Card momentum can now take down a well-rested heavyweight.
With a chance to reset between rounds, the best-of-five ALDS and NLDS matchups begin Saturday. Who will advance to the championship series?
With Wild Card matchups in the rearview mirror, The Sporting News predicts the 2026 MLB division series matchups.
MORE: Complete MLB playoff schedule for 2026 postseason
No. 6 Chicago White Sox vs. No. 2 Cleveland Guardians
You can certainly debate whether the Guardians (85 regular-season wins) or White Sox (84 regular-season wins) really belong on the postseason stage this season, with neither AL Central squad owning a ton of big-name star power. Regardless, the fact is that Cleveland and Chicago both find themselves with an opportunity to make a serious postseason run in a weaker AL bracket — and the White Sox have already taken advantage.
Chicago enters the ALDS the momentum of its first postseason series win since the 2005 World Series, proving in the Wild Card round that it has the power and pitching depth to challenge opponents. Cleveland, though, has better top-end starting pitching in Parker Messick, Gavin Williams and Tanner Bibee.
These two teams are well familiar with each other; the White Sox won the season series, 7-6. Cleveland's offense isn't very threatening, ranking last among all postseason teams in team OPS (.696) — this matchup will likely come down to how early the White Sox's bats can get to Guardians starters.
Saturday will mark the first time in MLB history that the Chicago White Sox and Cleveland have met in the postseason.
The White Sox began playing baseball in 1894 as the Sioux City Cornhuskers.
The Guardians began playing baseball in 1896 as the Columbus Buckeyes/Senators.
The fact that this is a divisional matchup means it will likely be close, but Chicago's momentum is hard to ignore, and there was only a one-win discrepancy between the sides in the regular season. The White Sox are finally building something serious, seemingly with a new hero every night. The power in Will Venable's lineup is dangerous enough to reach the ALCS.
Prediction: White Sox in 4
No. 4 New York Yankees vs. No. 1 Tampa Bay Rays
It's been clear since the start of the postseason that whichever AL East team emerged from the lower half of the bracket would be favored to reach the World Series. This is the heavyweight matchup of the two ALDS series, featuring elite starting pitching on both sides and some of MLB's premiere sluggers.
Of course, the massive question lingering over this matchup is how much, if at all, Aaron Judge will play for the Yankees. Even as the lower seed, if he's near 100 percent, it's hard not to view New York as the favorite to reach the ALCS; a healthy Judge, alongside Cody Bellinger, Luis Garcia Jr. and Ben Rice, takes Aaron Boone's lineup to a new level, capable of matching the all-around offensive excellence of Tampa Bay's quartet: Caminero, Yandy Siaz, Jonathan Aranda and Chandler Simpson.
The Rays won this season series 7-6, but it may be the most evenly matched division series. Both sides can roll out a trio talented starters — New York with Cam Schlittler, Max Fried and Gerrit Cole, and Tampa Bay with Drew Rasmussen, Nick Martinez and Shane McClanahan — to pair with deep offenses.
Yankees can line up their pitching as follows against the Rays:
Game 1: Gerrit Cole
Game 2: Cam Schlittler
Game 3: Max Fried
Game 4: Gerrit Cole
Game 5: Cam Schlittler
For two reasons, the Yankees are the pick here. For one, between Schlittler and arguably the best bullpen in baseball, New York is loaded with leverage arms. And the Yankees are also riding high off a dominant Wild Card series, biding time for Judge and Giancarlo Stanton to heal. Assuming those two sluggers can at least be used in some key at-bats, the Yankees' lineup is capable of changing games in an instant.
Prediction: Yankees in 5
No. 3 Atlanta Braves vs. No. 2 Los Angeles Dodgers
The Dodgers' path to becoming the first National League team to win three-straight World Series will begin with a matchup against a 94-win Braves squad fresh off a Wild Card win over the Phillies.
Los Angeles' rest advantage could be significant. Even if he's not pitching, Ohtani has been dealing with lingering injury concerns over the last few months. A week off between his last regular season game should only benefit him, not to mention the Dodgers' ability to line up their loaded starting rotation however they choose. With the Braves using Chris Sale in two games against Philadelphia, he may not be available early in the NLDS.
The Dodgers and Braves have built quite the postseason history. 👀🔥
2013 NLDS — LAD def. ATL
2018 NLDS — LAD def. ATL
2020 NLCS — LAD def. ATL
2021 NLCS — ATL def. LAD
2026 NLDS — ??? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/mHhbDO9gDX
The top of Atlanta's lineup is potent enough to make this an interesting series, and the team did beat the Dodgers five times in the regular season, but Ronald Acuna Jr., Austin Riley and Ozzie Albies will have to meet the moment in the NLDS. Yoshinobu Yamamoto has pitched well against Atlanta in his career, as have Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow.
Even if the Braves' bats can keep things close, it's hard to imagine Atlanta's pitching staff beyond Sale being able to contain Ohtani, Freddie Freeman, Kyle Tucker and Mookie Betts over a five-game series. The Braves are a good team, but the Dodgers are far too talented to fall this early in the bracket.
Prediction: Dodgers in 4
No. 4 San Diego Padres vs. No. 1 Milwaukee Brewers
This matchup pins baseball's best team all season, Milwaukee, against one of its hottest over the past month, San Diego. While the Brewers are the clear favorites here, between the best starting pitcher in the game this season and a deep lineup that plays to contact, the Padres do pose some interesting challenges, going 4-2 against Milwaukee in the regular season.
On one hand, San Diego has stars made for October. As shown in the Wild Card round, when the top of the Padres' lineup is on, they're a hard team to beat — Fernando Tatis Jr., Manny Machado, Xander Boegarts, Ty France and Jackson Merrill can look like one of the best 1-through-5 groups in baseball at times. Add in an elite starter (Michael King) and a strong bullpen led by Mason Miller, and there's a path for the Padres to pull off a stunner here.
Most data has shown that the more of a threat a team is to hit the ball out of the yard, the better they'll fare in the postseason. If this is finally going to be the year the Brewers reach a World Series — putting an end to their cycle of regular season success with playoff shortcomings — they'll need to slug more. This is an offense that's outstanding at making contact and getting on base, but has also continually come up short in October and finished second-to-last in team home runs (154) in the 2026 regular season.
Chances are, Milwaukee won't only be able to rely on its strong pitching staff to reach the World Series. The Brewers' bats will need some extra-base hits. But with the Padres' lackluster starting pitching depth, this is still a series the Brewers can claim even if they're not pristine.
San Diego may have some top-end talent and momentum, but the Padres can't match Milwaukee's all-around depth.
Prediction: Brewers in 4

item.description: Sale pitched 1.1 scoreless innings to close out Atlanta's victory over Philadelphia in Game 3 of the NL Wild Card Series on Thursday. He allowed one hit and no walks while striking out three. Sale threw 95 pitches during Atlanta's Game 1 win, and he returned to the mound only two days later to eliminate the division-rival Phillies. item.content:encoded:
Sale pitched 1.1 scoreless innings to close out Atlanta's victory over Philadelphia in Game 3 of the NL Wild Card Series on Thursday. He allowed one hit and no walks while striking out three.
Sale threw 95 pitches during Atlanta's Game 1 win, and he returned to the mound only two days later to eliminate the division-rival Phillies. The veteran left-hander induced five whiffs on 21 pitches Thursday as he made just his second relief appearance since the 2018 playoffs, when he worked out of the bullpen twice during Boston's World Series run. Even without the relief appearance, Sale would have been on short rest to start Game 1 of the NLDS against the Dodgers on Saturday, which makes him a logical candidate to pitch Sunday in Game 2, especially since that would still him up for a potential winner-take-all Game 5.

item.content:encoded:
Nola started the Phillies' 6-2 loss to the Braves in Game 3 of the NL Wild Card Series Thursday night at Truist Park. The veteran righty struggled with command early, allowing two one-out walks in the first inning before surrendering a three-run homer to Michael Harris II.
Nola settled down a bit in the second, quickly notching the first two outs. But after a single from Dominic Smith, Nola was lifted for reliever Tim Mayza. He threw 38 pitches in 1 2/3 innings, 19 of which were strikes.
The Phillies entered Thursday night expecting almost everybody else on their pitching staff to be available to help because it was win or go home.
Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly, pitching coach Caleb Cotham and other team officials gathered more than an hour after Wednesday’s dramatic, come-from-behind 4-3 victory over the Braves in 10 innings in Game 2 to talk about their Game 3 pitching plans. Mattingly indicated on Monday that Nola was working toward starting Game 3.
Ultimately, Nola was the most rested starter, so that’s why they chose him.
“Obviously it's another elimination game,” Mattingly said. “I think three out of the last four have been elimination games, so I'm assuming it'll be pretty much all hands on deck.”
Zack Wheeler started Sunday’s regular-season finale, the Phillies’ first of three elimination games this week. Wheeler, who threw 97 pitches Sunday, threw 68 over four frames after entering in the third inning of Thursday night's game.
The thought of Wheeler not pitching in a postseason series seemed impossible.
Left-hander Jesús Luzardo, who started Game 1 on Tuesday, said he would be available in the bullpen. He discreetly moved to the Phillies’ bullpen late in Game 2, just in case his team needed him. Rookie right-hander Andrew Painter tossed three scoreless innings of relief to win Game 2. He also said he would be available.
“Yeah, everything on the line,” Painter said. “Luzardo would make fun of me if I didn't. I'm 23. He says I should be good every day.”
After Duran played catch on Wednesday afternoon, he gestured with his hand that he felt iffy, but he said he hoped to feel better after receiving pregame treatment.
He didn’t improve enough to pitch Wednesday, but he pitched in the eighth inning Thursday night, striking out two.
Nola last pitched on short rest on Saturday against Tampa Bay, allowing four hits and three runs in one inning in a 12-1 loss. But after posting a 6.04 ERA in 17 starts through June 29, he had a 3.12 ERA in his final 15 starts before Sunday.
Nola had a 4.50 ERA in three starts against Atlanta during the regular season.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Joey Votto's Zack Wheeler proclamation goes hilariously wrong in Phillies-Braves Game 3
item.dc:creator: Jack Baer
item.description: Game 3 of the only wild-card series remaining on Thursday went very well for the Atlanta Braves. It did not go well for the Philadelphia Phillies. And it went particularly badly for NBC broadcaster and Cincinnati Reds great Joey Votto in one moment. item.content:encoded:
Game 3 of the only wild-card series remaining on Thursday went very well for the Atlanta Braves. It did not go well for the Philadelphia Phillies.
And it went particularly badly for NBC broadcaster and Cincinnati Reds great Joey Votto in one moment.
Votto helped call the game as an "Inside the Pitch" analyst, a field-level role in which he offered analysis throughout the game. He popped up in the fourth inning to praise the form of Philadelphia Phillies pitcher Zack Wheeler, who to that point had gotten four out of five batters out while his team trailed 3-0.
The praise was rather aggressive:
"As good as Zack Wheeler looks — this game is as in play as it gets — I do not see the Braves scoring any more runs the rest of the way."
Joey Votto learning about the Broadcaster Jinx in real time. 😂
"I do not see the Braves scoring any more runs the rest of the way." pic.twitter.com/iGhyj5sSJe
You probably know where this is going.
In the span of the next five pitches, Wheeler walked Austin Riley, then gave up a two-run homer to Braves second baseman Ozzie Albies in a massive blow to the Phillies. It took the Braves only two batters to prove Votto wrong.
And that's why on-air predictions are typically a bad idea for broadcasters. The NBC booth at least had fun with the moment, with color commentator C.J. Nitkowski telling Votto, "Joey, I've had a lot of fun working with you over these three days, but don't check your mentions."
Wheeler, who was pitching on short rest, finished the game with a line of 4 innings pitched, 3 hits, 2 runs, 3 walks and 3 strikeouts.
As you would imagine, Braves fans quite enjoyed the turn of events. That Albies homer gave Atlanta a significant cushion for the rest of the game, which ended in a 6-2 Braves victory to set up an NLDS clash with the Los Angeles Dodgers starting Saturday.
Votto, famed for his baseball IQ as a player, is in his first season with NBC Sports, which landed a significant MLB rights package that began this season. The network brought in Votto, Anthony Rizzo and Clayton Kershaw as part of an effort to strengthen its broadcast teams with players who only recently retired.

item.title: [MLB.com] Kerr, Holmes shine in Braves' Wild Card-clinching win

item.description: ATLANTA -- Ray Kerr was the left-handed reliever the Braves chose to get through Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper during the first inning of Game 3 of the National League Wild Card Series against the Phillies. item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA -- Ray Kerr was the left-handed reliever the Braves chose to get through Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper during the first inning of Game 3 of the National League Wild Card Series against the Phillies.
Kerr served as the opener in Thursday's series-clinching 6-2 win and dazzled, keeping the Phillies in check with 3 1/3 scoreless innings, allowing one hit and one walk with two strikeouts. Grant Holmes followed Kerr and allowed one run on two hits and one walk, while earning the win.
“This was just another Thursday,” Kerr said. “Growing up, I had a hard time. So, this was nothing.”
The Braves provided a clue they would go this way in Miami on Friday, when they used Kerr as an opener on Holmes’ scheduled start date.
“That was a best-case scenario, and [Kerr] did it,” Weiss said. “He got through the top twice, which kept us from using another guy at the top. So, Ray -- it all started with Ray. Everything fell into place because of Ray Kerr.”
Kerr posted a 1.47 ERA over 18 1/3 innings in nine appearances going back to his Aug. 17 season debut. Left-handed hitters were 4-for-23 (.174) against him in the regular season, with one extra-base hit, a double.
Kerr made two appearances against the Phillies in September, with the most recent a three-inning outing on Sept. 13. He got Schwarber to ground into a double play and then struck out Trea Turner to end the fifth. Harper began the sixth with a double but was left stranded.
Kerr has made just 19 big league appearances since the start of 2024. After tossing three scoreless innings against the Marlins on Friday, he said he would gladly welcome the chance to be an opener in the postseason.
Holmes posted a 3.57 ERA in 29 starts this season and a 2.94 ERA over his final 14 starts. Opponents produced a .590 OPS against him the first time facing him in a game and an .886 OPS during the second plate appearance.

item.title: [reviewingthebrew.com] How Brewers starters Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson fared against the Padres this year
item.dc:creator: Owen Jonas
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers will begin their first-ever postseason matchup with the San Diego Padres on Saturday night in what is bound to be an electric series between the two hottest teams in baseball. item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers will begin their first-ever postseason matchup with the San Diego Padres on Saturday night in what is bound to be an electric series between the two hottest teams in baseball. The Brewers, winners of 103 games during the regular season, secured the top overall seed in the postseason for the second consecutive year and are spending the week resting and preparing for what is hopefully a lengthy playoff run. The Padres, meanwhile, who tied the Brewers for the best regular season record during the month of September (18-6), hosted the Chicago Cubs in the Wild Card Series over the last two days, and swept the Brewers' rivals while outscoring them 12-1.
NL Cy Young front-runner Jacob Misiorowski will unsurprisingly start Game 1 for the Brewers on Saturday night and rookie right-hander Logan Henderson will more than likely start Game 2. Manager Pat Murphy noted that Henderson's Game 2 assignment is "subject to change," during a media session on Tuesday afternoon.
While the Brewers are known to pull tricks from their sleeves during the postseason, it's likely Murphy was referring to the possible use of a left-handed opener for Game 2 if Milwaukee ended up facing the Chicago Cubs, who had lefties Pete Crow-Armstrong and Michael Busch at the top of their lineup. Seeing as the Padres are more righty-heavy at the top of their order, with All-Stars Fernando Tatis Jr. and Manny Machado both hitting from the right side, it's more likely Henderson will serve as a traditional starter in Game 2 now that the Brewers are officially facing San Diego.
The Brewers didn't play their best baseball against San Diego this year, with a 2-4 record against the Friars to prove it, but interestingly enough, both Misiorowski and Henderson turned in strong performances against San Diego during the regular season. Let's take a closer look at the starts that Milwaukee's Game 1 and 2 starters made against their NLDS opponents during the regular season.
Both Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson tossed quality starts against the Padres during the regular season
Let's start with Misiorowski's outing against the Padres, which occurred way back on May 13. After back-to-back scoreless outings against the Washington Nationals and New York Yankees to start the month of May, Miz drew the middle contest of a three-game set against the Padres at American Family Field. Misiorowski, as he did throughout the 2026 campaign, dominated his competition, covering seven scoreless innings with 10 strikeouts while allowing just four hits.
It's important to note that the lineup Miz faced back in May looks slightly different than the one San Diego is rolling out in October, but Tatis, Machado, Jackson Merrill, Ty France, Gavin Sheets, and Xander Bogaerts all played in the May 13 contest. Tatis did collect two hits off Misiorowski, but one was an infield single on a play third baseman Luis Rengifo probably should have made, and the other was a bloop single that left the bat at 69.7 mph. The other two hits Miz allowed were also singles -- one a softly hit liner from France that Brice Turang nearly made a play on, and the other a rope to center from Sheets.
It's safe to say Misiorowski carved up the Padres when he faced them in May, but, as previously mentioned, the circumstances have changed. No offense is hotter than the Padres' right now, meaning the Brewers' flame-throwing ace will certainly be tested on Saturday night.
Henderson's start against the Padres was far more recent. The rookie right-hander was tasked with the series opener in San Diego on August 10, and therefore faced a Padres' lineup that more closely resembles the one he will see on Sunday afternoon. Henderson turned in a quality start in that mid-August outing, allowing three earned runs in 6.1 innings pitched, but did surrender two homers. One was a second-inning mistake to France -- Henderson left a changeup up in the zone and the Padres' first baseman hit a line drive homer just over the fence in left field. The other was a two-run shot from Merrill in the bottom of the seventh, when Henderson was facing the Padres' outfielder for a third time. It's important to note that Henderson most likely won't be asked to face the Padres' lineup three times on Sunday.
Even still, Henderson racked up seven strikeouts during his regular season start against the Padres, while allowing just five hits and one walk. His three earned runs tied the most he's allowed in a start, but continued his incredible streak of 23 straight starts to begin his MLB career in which he's allowed three earned runs or less. That consistency and ability to keep his team in the game is exactly what the Brewers need from Henderson in the postseason.
Ironically, despite impressive performances from their starting pitchers, the Brewers lost both Misiorowski and Henderson's starts against the Padres this year. The loss in Miz's start was due to an uncharacteristic performance from Abner Uribe in the ninth inning, whereas Henderson was handed the loss in his start after the offense couldn't rally for more than two runs. Similar starts from both Miz and Henderson this weekend would undoubtedly give the Brewers a good chance to build a 2-0 series lead before heading to San Diego for Game 3.

item.content:encoded:
Cubs rumors: Chicago insider dumps cold water over any potential Tarik Skubal free agency pursuit appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Chicago Cubs saw their season comes to an end Wednesday night when they were eliminated from the Wild Card round of the National League playoffs by the San Diego Padres. The Cubs lost the series in consecutive games after earning a spot in the postseason in the final days of the season.
While their time in the postseason was short-lived, the Cubs had multiple winning streaks in the early part of the season that allowed them to challenge the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Central Division. However, the Cubs could not match Milwaukee's consistency throughout the year, and they finished 14 games behind the Brewers.
The Cubs will almost certainly have multiple changes to their roster when the 2027 season gets underway. The Cubs have multiple free agents, including outfielders Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki as well as pitcher Shota Imanaga.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
However, the Cubs are not likely to get involved in the bidding for the top free agent expected to be available. Tarik Skubal of the Dodgers is expected to receive the top contract offer ever made to a pitcher in MLB history.
Skubal was traded by the Detroit Tigers to the Dodgers this summer. Skubal is represented by top player agent Scott Boras, and Skubal is a two-time Cy Young Award winner.
While a number of teams may get involved in the bidding for Skubal, an insider with ties to the Cubs does not believe the team will make a significant bid for the dynamic 29-year-old left-handed pitcher.
The Cubs have already committed about $110 million to future player contracts in 2027.

LOS ANGELES — The full schedule for the Division Series round was announced by Major League Baseball on Thursday, giving us the start times for potentially all five games of the Dodgers' first postseason round.
The Dodgers will play the winner of Thursday night's Braves-Phillies wild card battle in Atlanta, with their NLDS opening up at 1 p.m. Saturday at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles, a game televised by Fox. Game 2 on Sunday night is an FS1 game that starts at 5 p.m.
When the series shifts to the Eastern time zone, Game 3 on Tuesday will be televised at 3 p.m. PT, with Wednesday's Game 4 also starting at 3 p.m. PT, if necessary. Both Games 3 and 4 will be televised by FS1.
If there's a Game 5 in the Dodgers' NLDS, it will be back at Dodger Stadium on Friday, October 9, with a 5 p.m. PT start time on Fox.
Joe Davis and the No. 1 Fox Sports MLB crew will call this series.

item.content:encoded:
If you want more Action Network content, be sure to add us as a preferred source on Google.
The Atlanta Braves host the Philadelphia Phillies in Game 3 of their NL Wild Card Series on October 1, 2026. First pitch from Truist Park is scheduled for 8:00 p.m. ET. The game will be broadcast on NBC/Peacock.
The Phillies are favored by -115 on the moneyline and by -1.5 on the run line (+155). The Braves are -105 on the moneyline and +1.5 on the run line (-190). The total is set at 7.5 (+100o / -120u).
Find my Phillies vs Braves prediction for Game 3 below, as well as probable pitchers, starting lineups, the weather forecast and more.
My Phillies vs Braves best bet is on Philadelphia to win outright. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live MLB odds page, and download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis.
Phillies vs Braves Odds
- Phillies vs Braves moneyline: Phillies -115, Braves -105
- Phillies vs Braves over/under: 7.5 (+100o / -120u)
- Phillies vs Braves spread: Phillies -1.5 (+155), Braves +1.5 (-190)
Phillies vs Braves Preview, Starting Lineups
Phillies Game 3 Lineup
- SS Trea Turner
- 2B Bryson Stott
- LF Bryan De La Cruz
- 3B Edmundo Sosa
- C J.T. Realmuto
- CF Justin Crawford
The best three words in sports are "Win or go home". Everything is on the line here after the Phillies rallied to win Game 2. Their season was on life support until Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper hit back-to-back homers to tie the game in the 7th, and Alec Bohm hit the go-ahead homer in the 10th.
The burning question for manager Don Mattingly: Who pitches? Zack Wheeler or Aaron Nola? The answer feels obvious: go with Wheeler, the staff's ace. It would be four days between starts and three days of rest for Wheeler.
Wheeler boasts a 3.00 ERA, a 2.86 xERA, and a 3.35 FIP. He's a strikeout machine, punching out 10.72 per nine, but his walk rate has grown to 2.61 this year. He's rounding into prime form at the best time, pitching to a 1.71 ERA in five September outings.
Diving into the Phillies' pen usage, everything is on the table. The Phillies can add two extra weapons to their pen, with Aaron Nola and Jesus Luzardo as options. Andrew Painter threw 37 pitches in game two — so he might not be an option for Mattingly. The good news? Jhoan Duran will be an option since Painter saved the pen on Wednesday.
Offensively, the Phillies looked rough in the stretch entering the playoffs, but all it takes is one or two long balls to shift this game in their direction.
So far in the Wild Card round, Alec Bohm has been the guy for the Phillies, leading them with a .375 average and a 1.319 OPS. Schwarber and Harper are always a threat, but Bohm playing this well gives Philly a boost.
Braves Game 3 Lineup
- RF Ronald Acuña Jr.
- CF Michael Harris II
- SS Mauricio Dubón
- LF Mike Yastrzemski
- 3B Austin Riley
- 2B Ozzie Albies
- DH Dominic Smith
While the Phillies have multiple strong starter options for a do-or-die Game 3, the Braves have zero rotation depth, and it's showing. The options are a full bullpen game or an opener before Grant Holmes, or Grant Holmes on a short leash.
None of those are ideal options in this spot. The basic stats indicate Holmes had a solid year, posting a 3.44 ERA, but his 5.04 xERA and 4.67 FIP are terrifying in a playoff game. Holmes isn't a swing-and-miss pitcher, striking out just 6.8 hitters per nine innings, and when you can't strike hitters out, they get more chances to do damage.
Holmes also gets hit very hard, ranking in the 1st percentile in average exit velocity and third in hard-hit rate.
In this series, the Braves bats have been more reliable than the Phillies in the middle-to-bottom of the order. However, the top of the order has destroyed them. It starts with Ronald Acuna Jr. with no hits, Drake Baldwin hitting .222, and Matt Olson hitting .125.
Putting it lightly, the Braves will face an uphill battle winning this game if their three best hitters don't hit.
Sure, the Phillies totally limped into the playoffs, but the Braves have some glaring issues of their own, and they're showing up at the worst time. The lineup has been unreliable, and the rotation is a mess.
I want Wheeler or even Nola if he's starting. The Braves have no pitching answers to contain the Philadelphia big boppers.
Take the pitching and road team on the moneyline.

item.content:encoded:
Ian Happ, Seiya Suzuki, Shota Imanaga sound like guys who won't be with Cubs much longer appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Chicago Cubs saw their season come to an abrupt conclusion Wednesday night when they lost their second consecutive game to the San Diego Padres in the Wild Card round of the National League playoffs.
"Looking back at the 5 years, I don't know if I was able to reach the expectations that people had (for me) or for myself."
Seiya Suzuki hit 113 home runs as a Cub in his first 5 MLB seasons, behind only Ernie Banks (136) and Kris Bryant (138). pic.twitter.com/rzxffiIVtX
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
— Marquee Sports Network (@WatchMarquee) October 1, 2026
The Cubs had a streaky regular season, often showing their dominance in the first half of the season with notable winning streaks, but they were unable to keep up with the Milwaukee Brewers in the NL Central. They finished in second place to the Brewers, a full 14.0 games behind Milwaukee. They didn't clinch their playoff spot until the final days of the regular season.
Chicago ended the year and entered the postseason as the No. 5 seed in the National League playoffs. They had to go on the road to play the Padres. That proved to be a big disadvantage, because the Padres were among the hottest teams in Major League Baseball as the postseason got underway.
There could be significant changes on the Cubs roster as the team prepares for the 2027 season. Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki, two veteran mainstays in the Cubs lineup, will be free agents in 2027 and it seems quite likely that both will be with new teams when the upcoming season gets underway.
Happ spoke in the locker room and it sounded like he was saying goodbye to the organization. "All I can say is that I love being a Cub," Happ said, per the Marquee Sports Network. "I've loved my time. I've loved the place, the people, Wrigley Field, the fanbase. And it's been truly special. I don't think there's a better place in baseball to play."
Pitcher Shota Imanaga will also be a free agent in the offseason, and he may not figure in the team's pitching plans for the future.

Machado and the Padres defeated the Cubs in two games to advance to the National League Division Series. San Diego will now face the top-seeded Milwaukee Brewers in a best-of-five series. Although San Diego will be the underdog in this upcoming series, Machado is poised to have three more champagne celebrations in October. “We’re not done,” Machado said in the postgame loc
item.content:encoded:
San Diego Padres star third baseman Manny Machado is ready for more after sweeping the Chicago Cubs in the wild-card series.
Machado and the Padres defeated the Cubs in two games to advance to the National League Division Series. San Diego will now face the top-seeded Milwaukee Brewers in a best-of-five series.
Although San Diego will be the underdog in this upcoming series, Machado is poised to have three more champagne celebrations in October.
“We’re not done,” Machado said in the postgame locker room celebration. “We’re not done. We’re gonna continue to fight … to bring a championship to the city of San Diego.”
The Padres entered the 2026 postseason as one of the league's hottest teams, and they proved it in two games.
"Man, we've been playing some really good baseball," Machado said. "Hopefully we can keep doing that."
The Padres handled the Cubs in dominant fashion.
Chicago entered the series leading the majors in runs. However, they score just once in 18 innings and mustered only eight hits. The Padres dominated the Cubs in front of their home fans, and the pitching did their part.
Padres ace Michael King started things off with a bang. In Game 1 of the series, King led the way with seven scoreless innings.
Padres starter Nick Pivetta and the bullpen picked up right where King left off on Wednesday night.
"We do have a strong bullpen, and even the guys we haven't used are very good pitchers also," manager Craig Stammen said. "That's going to be the strength of our team as we go through the postseason."
Can the Padres Pull Off an Upset Against the Brewers?
The Padres enter their series against the Brewers as underdogs with +150 odds to come out on top.
The Brewers are major favorites with -180 odds.
Milwaukee enters with the best record in baseball. Likely NL Cy Young winner Jacob Misiorowski leads the Brewers in this series.
The young ace will likely get two starts if the series goes the distance.
While this will certainly be the Padres' toughest test yet, they are as confident as ever to get the job done.
"Momentum’s the biggest thing in baseball," Padres center fielder Jackson Merrill said. "It doesn’t matter whether it’s a regular-season game or a postseason game. Momentum is everything. We know they’re a good baseball team. They play the game to win.
"But you know what? We’re a pretty good baseball team, too."

Ricardo Sandoval is a freelance writer with On SI. He is a graduate of California State University, Northridge, and specializes in sports writing, particularly in MLB, NBA and NFL. He previously worked with Newsweek and The Sporting News.

The Atlanta Braves are in a win-or-go-home scenario on Thursday night when they take on the Philadelphia Phillies in Game 3 of the Wild Card Series.
Both teams are playing for the right to punch their ticket to the NLDS and take on the defending World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers.
But first, they have to handle their business on Thursday night, and ahead of the matchup, Braves manager Walt Weiss made some notable changes to his starting lineup.
Braves Announce Ronald Acuna Jr. Change
In usual fashion for Weiss, he likes to switch up the top of his order from one game to the next with Drake Baldwin and Ronald Acuña Jr.
On Thursday, Weiss will do that again, moving Acuña Jr. down in the order to the two-hole, while Baldwin will move up and bat leadoff.

Looking at Game 3 for Braves
Acuña Jr. is due for a breakout game at the plate after going hitless in his first six at-bats across the first two games. However, he scored the first run of Wednesday’s game in the first inning and has also tallied two stolen bases.

Both pitchers could have fairly short leashes depending on their performances early on, and as expected, each team will do whatever it can to advance. That could mean emptying the bullpen if needed.

item.dc:creator: Owen Jonas
item.description: After sweeping the Chicago Cubs in the NL Wild Card Series, the San Diego Padres have officially punched their ticket to the NLDS, where a matchup with the top-seeded Milwaukee Brewers awaits them. It will be the Brewers and Padres' first-ever meeting in the postseason, and there are no two hotter teams in baseball right now. item.content:encoded:
After sweeping the Chicago Cubs in the NL Wild Card Series, the San Diego Padres have officially punched their ticket to the NLDS, where a matchup with the top-seeded Milwaukee Brewers awaits them. It will be the Brewers and Padres' first-ever meeting in the postseason, and there are no two hotter teams in baseball right now. The Brewers and Padres each posted a 18-6 record during the regular season portion of their September schedule, and San Diego added two more convincing wins over the Cubs this week.
While Brewers fans are relieved not to have to deal with the added stress that comes with facing the Cubs in the postseason, the Padres' recent performance undoubtedly has some fans wishing for a matchup with Craig Counsell's squad. That said, for as well as the Padres are playing right now, there are still certainly reasons for Brewers fans to be encouraged by the specific matchup. Let's take a closer look at three of the Padres' weaknesses and how they might come into play in the NLDS.
3 reasons Brewers fans should be encouraged by their NLDS matchup with the Padres
1. Question marks remain in San Diego's starting rotation
Heading into the postseason, the Padres' rotation was certainly their biggest weakness. With an elite bullpen and a surging offense, fans were unsure what San Diego would get from their starting staff in October. However, the duo of Michael King and Nick Pivetta, the latter of whom had a limited regular season workload this year due to an early-season elbow injury, dominated the Cubs in the Wild Card series, allowing just one earned run in a combined 10.1 innings. King's seven-inning shutout on Tuesday night did the heavy lifting, but Pivetta certainly impressed on Wednesday night as well.
However, even if King and Pivetta replicate their Wild Card performances in the NLDS -- likely in Games 2 and 3 -- questions remain in regard to the rest of San Diego's starting options. Trade deadline acquisitions Casey Mize, who is currently hurt, and Robbie Ray, who snuck onto the Wild Card roster but didn't pitch, haven't panned out as the Padres hoped they would. Long-time Los Angeles Dodger Walker Buehler also made the Padres' initial playoff roster, and is certainly a candidate to start a game, but his pedestrian 4.63 ERA in 32 starts this year doesn't necessarily scream "postseason starter." Not only will San Diego need King and Pivetta to repeat their incredible Wild Card performances in the NLDS, but they will also need another less obvious postseason starter to step up.
2. Padres' league-average infield defense bodes well for Brewers' offensive approach
The Cubs had an elite defensive unit in 2026, that much was obvious. In addition to Pete Crow-Armstrong's impressive performance in center field, the Cubs' infield of Alex Bregman (who was limited to DH in the Wild Card series due to a freak injury), Dansby Swanson, Nico Hoerner, and Michael Busch took away a number of would-be base hits thanks to their impressive range and sure-handedness. The Padres, while their infield unit is fine, by no means have the same elite ability to take away ground-ball base hits, and is therefore a better matchup for the Brewers' offense.
Manny Machado remains a strong defender when it comes to Outs Above Average (OAA), but his Defensive Runs Saved (DRS) total tells a different story. Ty France is a solid defensive first baseman, but the duo of Xander Bogaerts and Jake Cronenworth up the middle is below-average in the field. It's an important part of this series because the Brewers rank first in MLB in Batting Average on Balls in Play (BABIP), third in infield hits, and second in bunt hits. In other words, Milwaukee puts a lot of pressure on opposing infield defenses, and the Padres' shaky unit could come back to hurt them in this series.
3. San Diego's offense was far closer to league average for a majority of the season
The Padres' offense is on fire right now. No team posted a higher collective batting average, slugging percentage, or wRC+ than the Padres during the month of September, and only the Brewers scored more runs. Strong final months from Fernando Tatis Jr., Jackson Merrill, France, and Bogaerts led the Padres to these impressive numbers during the month of September, but for a majority of the season, San Diego's offense looked far closer to league average.
From the start of the season to the end of August, San Diego held a collective wRC+ of 98, indicating that their offensive unit was below league average for the first five months of the season. During that stretch, they ranked 20th in home runs and 22nd in runs scored. Their strong final push made their season-long numbers appear far better, but for a majority of the 2026 season, San Diego's offense was not among the best in baseball. That could matter not if the Padres' recent hot streak continues throughout October, but it's important to note this recent performance is the exception, not the norm.
2 reasons Brewers fans should be nervous about their NLDS matchup with the Padres
1. The Padres are the hottest team in baseball (aside from maybe the Brewers)
Whether their recent performance is the exception or not, there's no denying that the Padres are one of the two hottest teams in baseball, with their only threat being the team they will match up against in the NLDS. As previously mentioned, the Brewers and Padres finished first and second, respectively, in runs scored during the final month of the regular season en route to MLB-best 18-6 records. The Padres then stymied a strong Cubs' team with two comfortable wins in the NL Wild Card Series.
For the Brewers, who seemingly run into the hottest team in baseball in the early rounds of the postseason every single year, a matchup with the Padres feels like more bad luck. San Diego surged to the top Wild Card spot in the NL, secured a home postseason series, swept said series, and now carries that momentum into the NLDS. That certainly doesn't feel like a fair draw for the best team in baseball, who just completed a record-breaking 103-win regular season. Yes, the Padres have more flaws on their roster than the Brewers, but sometimes all that matters is how a team is playing when the postseason rolls around, to which the recent performance of each of these two teams would suggest fans are in for a competitive series.
2. San Diego is the only team with a better bullpen than the Brewers
The Brewers are heading into the postseason with their bullpen at its best, which is not often the case following the 162-game season. The combination of Trevor Megill, Abner Uribe, and Aaron Ashby at the back end, trade deadline acquisitions JoJo Romero and Antonio Senzatela in the middle innings, and multi-inning options like DL Hall, Chad Patrick, and Shane Drohan has Milwaukee's relief corps among the best in baseball as the playoffs arrive.
However, if there's one bullpen group that is better than the Brewers', it's the Padres' ridiculous assembly of relief weapons. Flame-throwing closer Mason Miller and his elite set-up man Adrian Morejon rightfully garner much of the attention, but other arms like Bradgley Rodriguez, Jason Adam, who just returned from the 60-day IL, and southpaw Yuki Matsui deserve respect as well. Given the strength of San Diego's bullpen and the question marks in their rotation, the pressure will be on the Brewers to build early leads and take advantage of as many scoring opportunities as possible.

item.content:encoded:
In 1969, the San Diego Padres and Milwaukee Brewers — who were the Seattle Pilots for one season — were founded as MLB expansion teams.
Now, 58 short years later, the perennial National League contenders are meeting in the postseason for the first time.
On Saturday, Oct. 3, the best-of-five NLDS will get underway at Milwaukee’s American Family Field with the Brewers’ ace and Cy Young favorite Jacob Misiorowski (16-5, 1.80 ERA) on the hill.
Following a two-game stint in the Cream City, the series will move to SoCal for a pair of contests at San Diego’s PETCO Park. They’re slated to take place:
Game 3
Tuesday, Oct. 6
Game 4
Wednesday, Oct. 7
If you’d like to be there, tickets are available for both high-stakes hypothetical San Diego showdowns.
At the time of publication, the lowest price we could find on tickets for either game was $121 including fees on Vivid Seats.
Prices start at $99 including fees for the three potential meetings in Milwaukee.
Before this series, the Padres got revenge against the Chicago Cubs in the Wild Card round, sweeping MVP hopeful Pete Crow-Armstrong’s club at home after losing to them in three games to open the playoffs last year.
“They’re playing great baseball right now,” San Diego manager Craig Stammen said about his club.
Next up, they have a tall task taking on MLB’s winningest team in 2026.
Oddsmakers project the Brewers are -180 favorites going into the NLDS.
Yet, it should be factored in that San Diego took four of their six meetings over the course of the regular season including a clutch 4-3, eleven-inning victory on Aug. 12.
Is this the year that one of these two clubs finally gets over the hump and returns to the World Series?
While we can’t say for certain we do know that their first-ever postseason meeting with some of the game’s hardest flamethrowers in Misiorowski and Mason Miller should be downright electric.
Don’t miss this one. We just might have an instant classic on our hands.
For more information, our team has everything you need to know and more about the Padres vs. Brewers 2026 NLDS below.

item.content:encoded:
Willson Contreras shared his honest take on the Boston Red Sox's shortcomings after their Wild Card sweep by the New York Yankees, pointing to areas the team must improve.
The Red Sox were eliminated from the 2026 MLB postseason after the Yankees swept them 2-0 in the American League Wild Card Series. The Yankees dominated the best-of-three series at Yankee Stadium, outscoring Boston 18-2 across the two games. In Game 1, the Yankees shut out Boston 9-0 behind a strong performance from Cam Schlittler, who threw 6.1 scoreless innings.
In Game 2, Max Fried dominated for six innings before the Red Sox briefly found some momentum when Contreras hit a solo home run in the sixth inning, snapping Boston's 26-inning postseason scoring drought. However, the Yankees quickly regained control and eventually secured a 9-2 victory to complete the sweep. Following the loss, Contreras shared his honest response during the postgame locker room interview.
When asked about what went wrong with the Red Sox offense down the stretch of the regular season and into the playoffs, he said:
"I'm not gonna answer it because, I don't wanna give my honest answer, but, we got eliminated, that's the bottom line. We got in here trying to win. We didn't produce, we didn't execute any part of the game, and that's why we lose. I mean, I know that we had a really good stretch," said Willson Contreras.
He added:
"I'm really proud of what we did in the past, like I said, we were able to turn the season around for sure, 100%, but that's not enough. It's not enough, and at the end of the day, you win games in the regular season to clinch the playoffs, but then falling short in the playoffs, it's tough."
Despite the disappointing ending, the 2026 season was a rollercoaster for Boston. After a 32-46 start that left them at the bottom of the AL, the team went on a historic second-half surge to secure a playoff berth.
What did Willson Contreras say after the Red Sox clinched a spot in the 2026 playoffs?
The Boston Red Sox clinched an American League Wild Card spot in the 2026 MLB playoffs on Sept. 20. Despite losing 5-1 to the Tampa Bay Rays, they secured a postseason berth after the Atlanta Braves defeated the Houston Astros. The Astros' loss officially eliminated them from contention and secured Boston's playoff spot.
Following the achievement, Willson Contreras reflected on the team's remarkable turnaround in an interview. Expressing his pride in the team and his belief in his teammates, he said:
"I'm really thankful, first of all, for playing for Boston. Thankful for the front office for asking me to come here and all of the good human beings that are here on this team. This is just the first step ahead. I just wanted to let everybody know that I'm proud of every one of you," said Willson Contreras.
He added:
"I did believe in my team. I did believe in everybody who was here. I never had a doubt that this team couldn't turn the season around. At one point, we were texting each other and I just said, 'Keep believing in ourselves.'"
Contreras played as a first baseman and designated hitter for the Red Sox in 2026, setting career highs in home runs and RBIs. He played 130 games during the regular season, recording 123 hits and 68 runs.

item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 30: Ronald Acuña Jr. #13 of the Atlanta Braves reacts after scoring against the Philadelphia Phillies during the first inning in game two of the National League Wild Card Series at Truist Park on September 30, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images)
There is a big time MLB playoff matchup on the National League side of the bracket on Thursday between the Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies.
While the Braves have welcomed star outfielder Ronald Acuña Jr.’s services through the first two games of the season, some spectators and patrons don’t believe he’s been very productive and are calling on him to have a signature moment on Thursday evening.
Across the first two games of the Wild Card series with the Phillies, Ronald Acuña Jr. is 0-for-6 with a run scored, two stolen bases, and two walks.
Being that he’s either going to be the Braves’ first or second batter when manager Walt Weiss reveals the team’s lineup, it’s understandable why Atlanta might need more from the top of their order.
Ronald Acuña Jr. Could Be Difference Maker in Phillies-Braves Game 3 of WC
Atlanta Braves fans are calling on Ronald Acuña Jr. to have a signature moment in game three of the team’s Wild Card matchup with the Philadelphia Phillies.
Here are some reactions across Braves Country on socials:
@StatsSAC: “It has been nearly 6 years and over 80 plate appearances since Acuna Jr. hit a postseason home run If you wanna talk about due, it’s Ronald And him being the superstar he is is best path to winning this series and having some sort of hope vs Dodgers”
Aaron Nola is set to start the game for the Phillies, and Acuña Jr. has had a lot of success off the right-hander.
@HammerTerritory: “The Braves haven’t won an elimination game since Ronald Acuña Jr.’s ROOKIE season.”
Even Braves reporter Mark Bowman got into the conversation about RAJ:
“Ronald Acuna Jr. had his fun with Phillies fans in September, but he has hit .200 (7-for-36) with 2XBHs (both doubles), a .606 OPS, nine strikeouts and five walks in 10 postseason games vs. Philly going back to 2022. He’s 0-for-6 w/ 2BB and 2Ks during the current series.”
It would be a huge boost for the Braves if Ronald Acuña Jr. could come up with a huge swing against whoever is pitching for Philly.

item.title: [MLB.com] Lights-out bullpen deployed to perfection in Padres' Wild Card Series clinch
item.dc:creator: Cole Bradley
item.description: SAN DIEGO -- The lights cut out, Korn’s “Blind” blared, the sellout Petco Park crowd rose to their feet roaring and Mason Miller seemingly spawned onto the mound for the start of the ninth inning. item.content:encoded:
SAN DIEGO -- The lights cut out, Korn’s “Blind” blared, the sellout Petco Park crowd rose to their feet roaring and Mason Miller seemingly spawned onto the mound for the start of the ninth inning. The game was over. The National League Wild Card Series was over.
But in reality, it had ended well before that.
This is exactly why Padres general manager A.J. Preller assembled the best and deepest bullpen in baseball, for nights like Wednesday.
“In the postseason, you’ve got to get a lot of great hitters out,” Preller said. “You’ve got to have a lot of answers in that bullpen.”
After starter Nick Pivetta departed in the fourth, Padres manager Craig Stammen fully unleashed his bullpen over the final 5 2/3 innings against the Cubs in Game 2. Bradgley Rodriguez, Jason Adam, Adrian Morejon and Miller proceeded to allow just three men to reach base and keep Chicago’s league-best offense scoreless to slam the door on a 4-1 victory and send the Padres to the NL Division Series for a best-of-five-series against the Brewers.
Michael King going seven scoreless innings in Game 1 and saving the key arms in the back end set the Padres up perfectly to lean on that group the following night. If the Padres got an early lead, Stammen wasn’t going to mess around with keeping Pivetta in longer than he needed to secure the series.
That’s exactly how things played out.
San Diego scored a pair of runs in the second before Pivetta -- who did his job in limiting the Cubs over 3 1/3 innings -- got the hook in the fourth after giving up an RBI single to Nico Hoerner. A one-run lead ballooned to three after Gavin Sheets’ pinch-hit homer in the bottom half of the inning. The ‘pen took care of the rest.
“Michael’s effort last night was phenomenal and that allows us to go out firing in the early part of the game today and get our best guys out there,” Miller said. “It puts us in a really confident position. We get a lead and we feel really good about it.”
Perhaps the most important aspect of the Padres’ performance in this series was shutting down the Cubs’ elite lineup, and specifically their top two hitters in Pete Crow-Armstrong and Alex Bregman. The former is coming off the seventh 40-40 season in baseball history and the latter posted a 1.010 OPS in the second half.
They collectively went 0-for-15 in the series with eight strikeouts.
It was quite the statement, but it’s exactly what the Padres have been doing all season. By innings, San Diego had the fourth-most used bullpen in the Majors (683 2/3) and it possessed the fifth-best ERA (3.53).
“It’s an incredible group, top to bottom,” Adam said. “It doesn’t matter the situation, it doesn’t matter the inning, everybody out there is ready to go at all times. Fourth inning, ninth inning, I don’t care who we put out there, I feel really confident the guy is getting the job done.”
Rodriguez was the first into the fray, the rookie right-hander who immediately became one of the best relief arms in the sport and has been dominant in high-leverage situations throughout the year. He played fireman in the fourth, escaping a bases-loaded jam to preserve Pivetta’s line before pitching a clean fifth that he capped with a strikeout of Seiya Suzuki on a changeup below the zone.
“We’ve always known that about Bradgley -- that his maturity level is beyond his years,” Padres pitching coach Ruben Niebla said. “He doesn’t rattle. He doesn’t get nervous. He trusts himself and is a confident guy. We’re able to put him in those situations very confidently, and he’s responded well to that.”
Adam got through a 1-2-3 sixth, then Morejon cruised through the seventh and eighth, allowing just one hit, a Tyrone Taylor single. Then the ball was handed to Miller, the most imposing reliever in the game, who struck out an insane 47.4% of the batters he faced this season and finished with a career-best 1.67 ERA and 38 saves.
He gave up a double to Hoerner but struck out a pair and got Carson Kelly to ground out to end it, sending the Padres to Milwaukee and the Cubs back home.
“It’s not about any individual, it’s about a group,” Miller said. “It’s about passing the ball to the next guy and getting us in the clubhouse with a win. I think it’s a lot of selfless guys down there.”
Now, the Padres get the top-seeded Brewers in the NLDS, another team with plenty of firepower in the bullpen. To defeat them, and anyone else standing in the Padres’ way this October, Wednesday will be the template.
And if it continues to pan out the way it did, that should scare the rest of the postseason field.
“We knew we had six innings we could cover,” Niebla said. “It worked out to perfection.”

item.title: [pinstripealley.com] MLB Playoff Roundup: Alec Bohm’s 10th-inning homer forces Game 3 against Braves
item.dc:creator: Peter Brody
item.description: What a way to sweep the Red Sox out of the playoffs! The Yankees brushed aside their inferior opponents, winning the two games by a combined score of 18-2. Every facet of their game was clicking — plate discipline, slug, bat-to-ball, two-strike hitting, situational hitting, base running, defense, and of course, starting pitching. It’s a winning recipe that leaves them in good stead for the upcoming ALDS date with Tampa. The Yankees weren’t the only team to eliminate their opponents from the post
item.content:encoded:
What a way to sweep the Red Sox out of the playoffs! The Yankees brushed aside their inferior opponents, winning the two games by a combined score of 18-2. Every facet of their game was clicking — plate discipline, slug, bat-to-ball, two-strike hitting, situational hitting, base running, defense, and of course, starting pitching. It’s a winning recipe that leaves them in good stead for the upcoming ALDS date with Tampa.
The Yankees weren’t the only team to eliminate their opponents from the postseason on Wednesday so let’s jump straight into the action!
AL Wild Card Series Game 2
Chicago White Sox 7, Houston Astros 3
(Chicago wins 2-0)
After just two games, I can’t think of any playoff participant who wants to face these White Sox. That is a sentence that no one could conceive of typing at the start of the season. Two seasons removed from suffering the most losses in MLB history and on the back of three straight losing campaigns, this upstart Chicago squad came out of nowhere to crash the postseason, starting with a two game sweep of the Astros in their own building.
They have done so by scoring early and often, the White Sox lineup a deep unit one-thru-nine with multiple ways to hurt you. They work deep counts, foul pitches off, draw walks, and can put the ball in play, but can also slug the ball out of the yard from almost any spot in the batting order. On Tuesday, they scored three unanswered runs in the first two innings to put the Astros on the back foot from the word go, and Wednesday continued the trend with the Southsiders hanging a four-spot before the home team had a chance to bat.
They had a 1-0 lead just five pitches into the game against Astros ace Hunter Brown, Sam Antonacci leading off with a double before Kyle Teel drove him home with a single. A fielding error by Nick Allen on a Miguel Vargas grounder put a pair on, and three straight singles by Andrew Benintendi, Tristan Peters, and Chase Meidroth plated three more runs with help from a Lucas Spence throwing error from center.
Credit to the Astros, they did not roll over after going down four in the first and slowly chipped into the White Sox lead. Jeremy Peña led off the bottom of the first with a booming home run that clattered off the left field wall just below the train tracks. Cam Smith hit one to almost exactly the same spot with two outs in the second. Jose Altuve narrowly snuck a solo shot into the Crawford Boxes to lead off the fourth and just like that, a 4-0 game had become a 4-3 thriller.
An inning later it looked like the Astros would pull of the improbable and complete the comeback. Smith was hit by a pitch, Peña singled, and Isaac Paredes walked to load the bases with two outs for Altuve. However, reliever Anthony Kay got Altuve to fly out to medium right field to strand all three ducks on the pond. That left the door open for the White Sox to swing the momentum back in their own favor and they did so immediately. Benintendi and Peters drew a pair of walks to open the sixth, prompting Joe Espada to call on Bryan Abreu out of the bullpen. Astros owner Jim Crane vetoed a trade of Abreu to the Twins in the final minutes of the deadline, and Abreu rewarded that faith by hanging a 3-1 slider to Meidroth, the second baseman crushing a three-run bomb to left to put the final nail in the Astros’ coffin.
After sweeping this rematch of the 2005 World Series, the White Sox advance to the ALDS where they will face the AL Central champion Guardians, first pitch of Game 1 scheduled for 1:00 p.m. ET on Saturday.
NL Wild Card Series Game 2
Philadelphia Phillies 4, Atlanta Braves 3
(Series tied 1-1)
The Phillies’ season was hanging by a thread until some late heroics by Kyle Schwarber, Bryce Harper, and Alec Bohm sent this thrilling series to a decisive Game 3. It was a pitchers’ duel early between two starters trending in opposite directions. Tyler Mahle entered his first career playoff start with a sub-two ERA after joining the Braves from the Giants at the deadline while Cristopher Sánchez posted an ERA above five in the month of September (though will still likely wrap up his second straight runner-up finish in NL Cy Young balloting).
The one thing the two starters do have in common is first inning struggles and that certainly played out in this game. Mahle allowed a leadoff double to Trea Turner and consecutive one-out singles by Bryce Harper and Alex Bohm to allow the Phillies to jump ahead, 1-0. However, Sánchez issued a leadoff walk to Ronald Acuña Jr., who promptly stole second and scored the tying run on a Matt Olson single.
Both starters settled in from there, trading zeroes for the next five innings, until things unraveled for Sánchez and his defense in the seventh. Sean Murphy worked a leadoff walk and Ha-Seong Kim reached on a bunt single to put a pair on with no outs. Drake Baldwin then clubbed what looked like a routine liner to right, but Harper misplayed it horrifically breaking in on the ball only to watch it sail over his glove and to the wall for what was ruled as an RBI double. Sánchez intentionally walked Ozzie Albies to load the bases, and Olson made him pay with a sac fly to double the Braves lead, 3-1.
What should have been a hammer blow to the Phillies morale did not play out as such. Schwarber immediately responded with a towering leadoff shot off lefty reliever Dylan Lee, and Harper atoned for his misplay by going back-to-back to retie the game, 3-3. That sent this game to extra innings, where the much-maligned Alec Bohm continued his redemption tour. Bohm was on the bubble of being non-tendered during the offseason, but the Phillies kept him around and drove in the first run of the series with an RBI double in the first inning of Game 1. The third baseman was the ultimate hero in this one, his opposite field solo homer off rookie Didier Fuentes in the 10th to keep the Phillies season alive and force a decisive Game 3.
San Diego Padres 4, Chicago Cubs 1
(San Diego wins 2-0)
This game featured surprisingly quick hooks of both starters as neither manager wanted to risk leaving their highest leverage relievers unused. One was certainly more deserved than the other, Kevin Gausman allowing three runs on five hits in 3.1 innings. The Cubs were desperate for starting pitching at the Trade Deadline and Gausman was supposed to be their big prize. However, he flopped after making the move from the Blue Jays, pitching to a 4.83 ERA in nine starts post-deadline, and his stinker tonight was the beginning of the end of the Cubs’ season. Nick Pivetta on the other hand held Chicago to a run on three hits and two walks with four strikeouts in 3.1 innings, but Craig Stammen seemed determined to play the matchups in this one.
Ty France got things started with a double to lead off the second, advancing to third on a Jackson Merrill single, who then stole second to put a pair in scoring position for Xander Bogaerts. The veteran shortstop opened the scoring with an RBI single, which brought Ethan Salas to the plate. The 20-year-old became the youngest catcher ever to appear in a playoff game, and in his first postseason PA, he lifted a sac fly to center to plate Merrill as the Padres’ second run.
The real story of this series has been the Cubs’ inability to score. They led MLB scoring 5.25 runs per game, spearheaded by shoo-in NL MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong and his MLB-leading 45 home runs (PCA would go 0-for-7 with four strikeouts in the series). They found themselves shut out through the first 12.1 innings of this series, finally breaking the seal in the fourth on a Seiya Suzuki single, Ian Happ walk, and Nico Hoerner RBI single. A Carson Kelly hit-by-pitch loaded the bases with two outs, but Dansby Swanson flew out to stand all three in place.
San Diego immediately punished them for failing to fully cash in on that scoring opportunity. Bogaerts reached on a one-out double, prompting Craig Counsell to call on Daniel Palencia in relief of Gausman. Palencia yanked a 101 mph fastball right into Sheets’ nitro zone down and in, and the lefty crushed it to right for a mammoth two-run blast.
It was all hands on deck from there from the Padres bullpen looking to protect their lead for the final five innings of the contest. They proved how terrifying a relief corps they’ve been all season, allowing just three base runners — a Michael Busch walk with two outs in the fifth, a Tyrone Taylor pinch-hit single with one out in the eighth, and a Hoerner one-out double off Mason Miller in the ninth — after the Cubs stranded the bases loaded to end the fourth.
San Diego advances to the NLDS where they will face the best team in baseball. It’s an unenviable position to come up against presumptive NL Cy Young Jacob Misiorowski and the 103-win Brewers. Game 1 of that series is scheduled for October 3rd with first pitch time contingent upon the result of Game 3 between Philly and Atlanta.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox were swept by the New York Yankees in the American League Wild Card Series, and Sonny Gray now faces a decision on his future.
Earlier this year, the 36-year-old pitcher noted that he is open to retiring if his family wants him to hang it up. He had a great year and revealed after the game that he thinks he has a lot of baseball left in him. However, he needs to decide if playing is what's best for him and his family.
"I was telling him that a second ago, whatever him and his family decide, it was a joy to watch this year," ace Garrett Crochet said after the loss to the Yankees, per MassLive's Chris Cotillo. "I still think he's got a lot to give the game, but there's something to be said about going out on your own terms, I suppose. Whatever he ultimately decides, that'll be something that as a team, we support him on. But it was a pleasure having him here in Boston."
Even if Gray continues to play, his postgame comments open the door for him to leave the Red Sox. He has a $30 million mutual option, which will likely be declined by the Red Sox. He could re-sign as a free agent, but when he was asked if Boston was a destination he would consider after the year he had, he said "I don't know."
Gray stepped up big time for the Red Sox this year. They needed the entire rotation to play better with Crochet hurt. Having him and Crochet together in the rotation, along with Payton Tolle and Ranger Suarez, would be great for the Red Sox.

item.content:encoded:
One of two National League Wild Card Series wrapped up on Wednesday night when the San Diego Padres completed their two-game sweep of the Chicago Cubs.
The series win for San Diego means it will hit the road and travel to the Midwest for an NLDS showdown against the 103-win Milwaukee Brewers.
The two teams met six times in the regular season, with the Padres taking four of six games from the Brewers. Let's dive into who performed well from each side in those six games.
Offensively for San Diego, it was a bit of an unlikely hero in the regular season series. First baseman Ty France was outstanding against the Brewers, slashing .389/.421/.556, good for an OPS of .977 with a homer and three walks.
Wednesday's playoff hero Gavin Sheets also was stellar against Milwaukee, slashing .308/.471/.589, good for an OPS of 1.009 with four walks and a game-winning home run early in the season.
The San Diego bullpen arms were also solid, especially Adrian Morejon and Mason Miller, who combined for five shutout innings across five appearances.
Ty France drills a solo home run to left field and cuts the Padres' deficit to 2-1 in the bottom of the 2nd!
Brewers @ Padres#MLB #ForTheFaithful pic.twitter.com/fzfv1Pd9GQ
GAVIN SHEETS 9th-INNING HEROICS
Down to their last out, the @Padres have rallied! pic.twitter.com/yO0CxqvN33
Milwaukee did not have much offensive success against San Diego, averaging just 3.5 runs per game. There were still encouraging signs, though, especially from the first base duo of Jake Bauers and Andrew Vaughn.
Bauers had 18 at-bats against the Padres, slashing .278/.381/.444 with three doubles and three RBI. Vaughn hit .294 with two RBI in 17 at-bats.
NL CY Young frontrunner and Game 1 starter Jacob Misiorowski made one start against the Padres in the regular season and it was excellent. Misiorowski tossed seven shutout innings with zero walks and 10 strikeouts. Left-hander Kyle Harrison was also good against the Padres, posting a 2.79 ERA across two starts and 9 2/3 innings.
10 strikeouts for Jacob Misiorowski
He completes 7 IP for the first time in 2026! pic.twitter.com/nsJoZX3DVp
Milwaukee has a slight advantage in the starting pitching department, but the two bullpens may be the deciding factor in the series.
They ranked first and third in the National League in ERA this season and the ultimate deciding factor may be which bullpen blinks first and lets a late lead slip away.

item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Braves will host the Philadelphia Phillies in a decisive Game Three of the National League Wild Card series tonight (Thursday, October 1). The winner will advance to face the Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Division Series (NLDS). The Braves won Game One, but the Phillies rallied to win Game Two on Wednesday (September 30), setting the stage for this winner-take-all contest.
The game will start at 8 p.m. ET and will be broadcast on NBC and Peacock. Spanish language coverage will be available on Universo and Univision Radio, while ESPN Radio will provide live national coverage of all 2026 MLB postseason games.
The Phillies' starting pitcher remains undecided, with options including Aaron Nola and ace Zack Wheeler. Meanwhile, the Braves may rely on Grant Holmes to handle the bulk of the innings, though they have not confirmed if he will start or follow an opener. Left-handers Ray Kerr or Brent Suter are potential openers.
Both teams have key players to watch. For the Phillies, Alec Bohm hit a game-winning homer in Game Two, while Bryce Harper and Kyle Schwarber hit back-to-back homers in the eighth inning to tie the game. On the Braves' side, Michael Harris II and Mauricio Dubón have been performing well at the plate.
The Phillies have a history of postseason success against the Braves, having defeated them in previous playoff series, including the 1993 NLCS and the 2022 and 2023 NLDS. The outcome of tonight's game will determine who advances to face the Dodgers in the next round.

item.content:encoded:
October baseball is upon us, and we have a massive playoff game on Thursday night.
The Philadelphia Phillies and Atlanta Braves are the only teams remaining in the wild card round, setting up a standalone Game 3 on Thursday night.
The Phillies came back from a 3-1 deficit in Game 2 – after a key Bryce Harper error – to win in extra innings behind solo shots from Harper, Kyle Schwarber and Alec Bohm.
The starting pitching matchup for Game 3 is murky at the moment, although two beat reporters gave some insight into what these teams might do.
Long-time Phillies reporter Jim Salisbury shared that he’s hearing veteran Aaron Nola will get the start for the Phillies while the Braves will go with an opener in Ray Kerr. The Atlanta bullpen is elite, ranking fourth in MLB in ERA during the regular season.
Braves beat reporter Mark Bowman also shared some insight to the starting pitching matchup, mentioning that Braves righty Grant Holmes could be used as the “bulk” option behind Kerr on Thursday. He also believes the Phillies will use a combo of Nola and ace Zack Wheeler, who would be pitching on short rest after leading the Phillies to a win on Sunday.
All hands are going to be on deck in this matchup for both teams, as this is a win-or-go-home scenario.
Oddsmakers have set the Phillies as slight favorites on the road, a sign that they have more confidence in Philly’s options to start in this game.
Here’s a breakdown of the odds, a player prop to bet and my prediction for Thursday’s Game 3.

- Braves +1.5 (-174)

- Braves: -102

Braves Best MLB Prop Bet
- Drake Baldwin OVER 1.5 Hits, Runs, RBIs (-108)
In today’s edition of Walk-Off Wagers – our MLB Best Bets column at SI – I shared why Baldwin is worth a look if Nola gets the start:
If Nola ends up getting the start, it’s a good sign for Braves catcher/designated hitter Drake Baldwin.
Baldwin picked up two hits and a run batted in on Wednesday, and he’s fared extremely well against Nola in his career.
The 25-year-old is 5-for-11 (.455) against Nola in his career, with a .955 OPS. He’s driven in one run against the Phillies veteran, and Nola has struggled quite a bit with the long ball this season, allowing 37 in 33 starts during the regular season.
A homer would immediately hit this prop for Baldwin, and he’s coming off a strong showing on Wednesday. During the regular season, the Braves star hit .284 overall and .307 against right-handed pitching.
Baldwin also entered the playoffs on a hot streak, batting .360 with two home runs, five runs batted in and a .951 OPS over the final two weeks (12 games). He’s a pretty interesting bet with this prop set at -108 on Thursday.
Phillies vs. Braves Prediction and Pick
Another play from today’s Walk-Off Wagers, I’m going to back the Phillies to win and advance after stealing Game 2:
There’s certainly an argument to be made for the Braves, who went 23 games over .500 at home in the regular season, but I lean with the Phillies in Game 3.
If Wheeler is able to pitch on short rest in any capacity, he’ll be by far the best pitcher in this game and had a massive finish to the regular season. Wheeler had a 1.71 ERA in September, lowering his season-long ERA to 3.00. He may not be able to give the Phils a ton of length, but it should help ease the pressure on their bullpen.
Nola has pitched in a ton of big games in his career, and I don’t want to downplay his two solid starts against Atlanta earlier this month. In two outings, Nola allowed just 10 hits and three earned runs across 13.1 innings of work.
The Braves have only used Kerr as an opener once this season, and Holmes had some very shaky advanced numbers in the regular season, ranking in the 12th percentile in expected ERA and the 18th percentile in expected BAA.
The Atlanta bullpen has been taxed in this series, pitching Didier Fuentes, Dylan Lee and Rasiel Iglesias in back-to-back days. That’s not nothing. Can the Atlanta ‘pen hold up after blowing Game 2?
I’d much rather take the Phillies and their proven veteran starters in a winner-take-all game, especially after they showed they can power themselves to a win on Wednesday.
Pick: Phillies Moneyline (-118 at DraftKings)
